## Webscraping 1

Assignment: Use rvest_wiki01.R to scrape foreign reserve date from Wikipedia!

1.  Download rvest_wiki01.R and download the packages!

library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(stringr)

2. The website in question (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_foreign-exchange_reserves)

3. Read the HTML! 
wikireserve<- read_html(url)

4. Need to tell R which table to grab
foreignreserve <- wikiforreserve %>%
  html_nodes(xpath = '//*[@id="mw-content-text"]/div/table[1]') %>%
  html_table()
  
5. Save the table! 
fores <- foreignreserve[[1]]

6. Rename the columns
names(fores) <- c("Rank", "Country", "Forexres", "Date", "Change", "Sources")



## Now we can modify the program to start scraping the tables provided in the website! 

foreignreserve2 <- wikiforreserve %>%
  html_nodes(xpath = '//*[@id="mw-content-text"]/div/table[2]') %>%
  html_table()


7. Cleaning up the dataframe: 

str(fores)

fores$newdate <- stringr::str_split_fixed(fores$Date, "\\[", n = 2)[,1]
fores$newdate <- trimws(fores$newdate)
fores$newdate_date <- as.Date(fores$newdate, format = "%d %B %Y")

newfores <- fores[-c(1, 2), ]

newfores_clean <- newfores %>%
  select(Country, Forexres, newdate_date)

newfores_clean <- newfores_clean %>%
  mutate(
    Forexres_clean = stringr::str_replace_all(Forexres, ",", ""),
    Forexres_clean = as.numeric(Forexres_clean)
  )


fx_reserves_final <- newfores_clean %>%
  select(
    Country,
    Forexres_clean,
    Date = newdate_date
  )

head(fx_reserves_final)
str(fx_reserves_final)
